clips.linkedin:
Give your AI your story and the publications your audience reads, and it finds who covers that subject now.

If nobody outside the company would mention your story to a friend, a press release won't change that.

That's Seth Godin's Purple Cow applied to PR. Only remarkable things get noticed. Our view is that most PR problems are really product or story problems, so the first job is finding something remarkable to say.

The second job is sending it to the right people. In Muck Rack's 2026 survey, 88% of journalists said they immediately disregard pitches that miss their beat. Give your AI your story and the publications your audience reads, and it reads each journalist's recent articles and hands back who covers the subject now, with two recent pieces each as evidence.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/pr-101-basics/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Godin's argument is that only remarkable things get noticed. A brown cow in a field is invisible, a purple one gets talked about. So the product or idea itself has to be worth remarking on. And the same test applies to a story. If nobody outside the company would mention it to a friend, a press release won't change that. Our view is that most PR problems are really product or story problems. So the first job isn't the pitch. It's finding something remarkable to say.

clips.linkedin:
Give your AI your story and the publications your audience reads, and it finds who covers that subject now.

In Muck Rack's 2026 survey of 897 journalists, 88% said they immediately disregard pitches that miss their beat. Most pitches go to the wrong person.

Give your AI the story in one sentence and a list of publications your audience reads. With browsing on, it reads each journalist's recent articles and hands back a table of who covers the subject now, with two recent pieces each as evidence.

Then have it test the story before anyone writes a release. It scores it against what journalists said they value, relevance, sources, original data and images, and tells you plainly if there's no news in it.

The prompts are in the show notes, with the full episode and article at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/pr-101-basics/ (the podcast voices are AI-generated).
clips.text: Get AI on this: building the beat list before you pitch. Give it the story in one sentence and a list of publications your audience reads, and with browsing switched on it reads each journalist's recent articles and hands back a table of who covers the subject now, with two recent pieces each as evidence. It drops anyone whose beat doesn't fit and says when it couldn't check. Second, get AI on testing whether the story is remarkable before anyone writes a release. Give it the story and the evidence behind it, and it checks it against what journalists said they value, relevance, sources, original data and images, scores each, and tells you what's missing. It'll tell you plainly if there's no news in it.
